meetings.headline: New Lunenburg planning director floated zoning fixes for small stores; Leominster briefed the committee on outreach.
meetings.summary: Leominster's economic development coordinator, Amanda Curtis, gave the Lunenburg Economic Development Committee an overview of Leominster's marketing, sponsorship, small-business grant, and infrastructure programs. Lunenburg's newly hired planning and economic development director, Stephen Wallace, introduced himself, proposed visitor-guide advertising and a business brochure, agreed to draft a "minor site plan review" process to ease zoning burdens on small storefronts, and, after consulting town counsel, confirmed non-restaurant businesses may allow BYOB without permission. No formal votes were taken except the roll-call adjournment.

attendees.role: new director of planning and economic development, Lunenburg
presenter, economic development coordinator, city of Leominster

votes.moved_by: a member (name not clear on captions)
votes.outcome: passed (roll call: Jean yes, Judy yes, Anna yes)

budget_items.what_was_said: Leominster's economic development coordinator said the city runs over 50 events a year with a zero dollars budget for those events, relying on sponsorships and donations.
During COVID, Leominster used ARPA funds for a facade improvement program reimbursing up to 75% of a project cost, with 14 building owners and businesses taking part.
A newsletter sponsor's funds have been redirected into small grants to local businesses, described as $250 grants so far, with hope the fund grows.
The coordinator said she keeps newsletter print runs conservative, printing about 200 copies to avoid waste, distributing the rest online.
The brook and culvert reconstruction project is under construction and grant-funded; FEMA reportedly prioritized it after the 2023 flood.

budget_items.topic: Large development project near Shirley Road
budget_items.what_was_said: A planning board member said an engineering firm plans a large multi-building project near Shirley Road totaling close to 900,000 square feet of floor space, made possible by an earlier water supply protection district bylaw.

decisions.decision: Stephen Wallace to draft a 'minor site plan review' process so simple changes of use in small existing storefronts (no parking increase, no building alterations) would not require full planning board site plan review; would need zoning language amendment for annual town meeting, or a planning board regulation amendment any time via public hearing.
Committee offered to form a sub-quorum working group (two members plus the ex officio member) to assist Stephen Wallace on the site plan review work if helpful.

After consulting town counsel, determined that non-restaurant businesses (e.g., a nail salon, hardware store) may allow customers to BYOB without needing town permission, since Lunenburg has no BYOB regulation for non-restaurant businesses.
Committee noted Lunenburg lacks an advertisement in the North Central Massachusetts visitor guide and should consider adding one to promote town events.

meetings.headline: New planning and economic development director hired for Lunenburg, starts February 2
meetings.summary: The committee learned the town has hired a planning and economic development director (Stephen Wallace, starting Feb. 2) and that PJ Keating has agreed to host the 2026 town official meet-and-greet at no cost to the committee. Most of the meeting was spent on a proposed bylaw to let non-restaurant businesses (prompted by a nail salon wanting to allow BYOB at bachelorette-party events) hold BYOB alcohol events, with no vote taken and the group deciding instead to meet with visiting town counsel the next day. The committee also set its February 10 agenda (an introduction from the new director, a town-counsel update, a business overview, and a presentation from Leominster's economic development office) and approved its December 9 minutes.

what_happened.line: The town has hired a planning and economic development director, Stephen Wallace, starting February 2.
The committee took no vote on a proposed bylaw letting non-restaurant businesses host BYOB alcohol events, deferring to a meeting with town counsel.
PJ Keating agreed to host the 2026 town official meet-and-greet, covering space, heat, tables and food at no cost to the committee.
The committee set its February 10 agenda: an introduction from the new director, a town-counsel update on the bylaw, a business overview, and a Leominster economic-development presentation.

why_it_matters: A new bylaw on BYOB alcohol events at non-restaurant businesses, prompted by a nail salon's request, would change what local businesses may host and requires town counsel review before any vote.
The new economic development director's start signals how the town staffs outreach to businesses, a service residents may interact with directly.
